tools.name: get_firm_overview
tools.description: What this company secretarial firm offers: the services a customer can start here (with the flow name the other tools take), whether it provides a virtual office address and a nominee director, its policy links and how the process works. Call this first.

tools.name: describe_flow
tools.description: The steps of one service's application, in order, each with the JSON Schema of the fields the customer fills in, and the stages after submission (payment, identity verification, signing, filing). Use it to know what to ask the customer.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: The packages and add-ons for one service, step by step, with prices in the firm's currency and the item ids estimate_quote takes. Some steps only apply under a condition (listed under conditions); pass flags to see the steps as that customer would.

tools.name: estimate_quote
tools.description: Price a selection of packages and add-ons for one service: one-time and recurring totals, tax and the grand total. Selections map a list_packages step slug to the item ids chosen on that step. Reports required steps left without a choice.

tools.name: check_company_name
tools.description: Whether a proposed Sdn Bhd name is already in use on this firm's platform (exact match only), what SSM's naming rules refuse in it (naming_problems: the name must change), and which words need an authority's approval (approval_warnings: allowed, the firm follows up). It is not an SSM name search: SS

tools.name: search_msic_codes
tools.description: Find five-digit MSIC 2008 business activity codes by what the business does (e.g. "software development", "online shop", "cafe") or by the first digits of a code (e.g. "620"). Each match says what the code includes, officially. Once company_details is saved, get_business_classification suggests code

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: The signed-in customer's applications with this firm, newest first: id, service, status and company name. Cancelled applications are left out.

tools.name: start_application
tools.description: Start the signed-in customer's application for a service, or resume their open draft for it. Returns the application id and its steps; fill them in with update_application_step.

tools.name: get_application
tools.description: One of the signed-in customer's applications: status, each step's saved answers and whether the step is complete or what to fix, and what to do next.

tools.name: update_application_step
tools.description: Save the customer's answers for one step of their application. Fields follow the step's JSON Schema from describe_flow; fields left out keep their saved values. Returns what to fix per field when an answer is refused, in which case nothing was saved.

tools.name: get_business_classification
tools.description: The drafted business description, company-name explanation and MSIC codes for an incorporation, for the customer to review before saving the business_classification step. The draft is made in the background after company_details is saved; poll while its status is pending.

tools.name: regenerate_business_classification
tools.description: Draft an incorporation's business description, name explanation and MSIC codes again, e.g. after the first draft failed or the customer wants fresh suggestions. Poll get_business_classification for the result.

tools.name: submit_application
tools.description: Submit the signed-in customer's finished application to the firm. Only call it after showing the customer the firm's terms and policies (get_firm_overview links them) and the declaration that the application is true and complete, and after they explicitly agree. tools.name: choose_package
tools.description: Choose the items on one checkout step of a submitted application, replacing that step's previous choice. Item ids come from get_checkout; an empty list clears an optional step. Returns the updated cart.

tools.name: create_handoff_link
tools.description: A link the signed-in customer clicks to continue on the firm's website, already signed in: "payment" to pay (after choosing packages), "verification" for identity verification, "signing" to sign documents, "documents" to upload a switch-in's documents. tools.name: cancel_application
tools.description: Cancel one of the signed-in customer's draft applications that was never submitted, freeing its company name. It can't be resumed afterwards. Only call it after the customer explicitly confirms.

tools.name: list_companies

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_business_classification, create_document_link · Private data: create_handoff_link, create_company_link, get_company_registers, find_company_documents, list_signing_requests, create_document_link · Public sink: submit_application, create_handoff_link, get_company_particulars.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_business_classification, create_document_link · Private data: create_handoff_link, create_company_link, get_company_registers, find_company_documents, list_signing_requests, create_document_link · Public sink: submit_application, create_handoff_link, get_company_particulars

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
